healthims.hims_employees.description: Master data, replaced whole each day. Unpartitioned: small, and no time dimension to prune on. A full replace leaves exactly one live file, so maintenance has nothing to compact here -- included deliberately, as the control case where the right answer is to do nothing.

healthims.hims_discharge.description: Partitioned by created_at, not updated_at: created_at is stable for a row's life, so a next-day restart rewrites inside the original partition instead of moving the row. Z-ordered because there are two independent access paths -- incremental reads filter updated_at, lookups filter process_id -- and a sort would only serve whichever key led.

healthims.hims_events.description: Partitioned by occurred_at so time-range queries prune to a day. Within the day, process-trace lookups filter process_id and sub-day slices filter occurred_at, so both are z-ordered. Alternative worth measuring: z-order(process_id, event_name), which trades sub-day time pruning for funnel-count pruning.
